proof.text: Apply the independent-universe bounded-flat K-flat criterion to the single complexes on Pm.Q and Pm.H. Their degree-zero terms are flat by the hypotheses, and all other terms are zero and hence flat; siteSheafTensorRightIso identifies site-flatness with the categorical tensor functor. Dmn.computes makes ordinarySingle invertible on both objects.

Conjugate the actual transitivity isomorphism by the normalized quotient identifications, and pull the resulting isomorphism back through DerivedCategory.singleFunctor.preimageIso after inverting ordinarySingle. For torsion use the fully faithful composite of the single functor and shift by one, inserting Dmn.T.commShiftIso. Functor.map_preimage and inverse cancellation prove the two displayed derived comparison identities. The comparisons are thus constructed from the actual transitivity morphism; no separate local tensor inverse is needed.

Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app gives the composite-unit characterization of the transitivity definition. Transport it across the normalized identifications using naturality of the two adjunction units. The chosen normalized sheaf adjunction on a flat single complex gives ordinarySingle_unit. Its proof uses the K-flat unit equation of sheafDerivedScalarAdjunction_exists, naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors and the degreewise identity for singleMapHomologicalComplex. Restriction-composition coherence on singles follows from mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac; its degreewise complex equality is checked at degree zero and between zero terms. The proved source-library Shift.ExactFunctor instances and the adjunction-induced commShift structure give the shifted versions.

Define the transpose kQ of the ordinary quotient comparison by the chosen ordinary scalar adjunction unit. Postcompose the composite-unit equation with the single restriction comparison. Use ordinarySingle_unit, naturality of the single restriction comparison and Identifications.quotient_unit at m and n. Faithfulness of the single functor yields Pm.p followed by the restriction of kQ and restrictionComp equal to eqToHom hF followed by Pn.p. The normalized ordinary unit sends x to the sheafification of 1 tensor x; linearity gives the formula on b tensor Pm.p(f).

Put d=m/n. Over the integer sheaf, lift d times Pm.i followed by eqToHom hB through the kernel Pn.kummer.exact, using nd=m and Pm.wi. This defines betaIntegral and proves its inclusion equation. The maps betaIntegral, d times eqToHom hB, and eqToHom hB form a morphism of the Kummer short complexes. ShortExact.singleTriangle.map.comm3 gives precisely Pm.kummer.singleDelta followed by the shifted single image of betaIntegral equal to the single image of eqToHom hB followed by Pn.kummer.singleDelta.

Let beta be the ordinary scalar-adjunction transpose of the constructed eH. Postcompose the shifted composite-unit equation with the restriction shift comparison and the shifted single comparison. Apply the shifted ordinarySingle unit formula and both Identifications.kummer_unit equations. Cancel the invertible shift and single comparisons, obtaining exactly the Kummer boundary square of the previous step for the integer restriction of beta. To identify the two maps, subtract them and apply Triangle.yoneda_exact2 to the twice rotated distinguished Kummer triangle. Their difference factors through the shifted single on the middle B. Full faithfulness of the shifted single functor represents that factor by a sheaf map B to the integer restriction of Pn.H. The latter is annihilated by n (use Pn.wi and monicity of Pn.i), hence by m. Multiplication by m on B is epi by Pm.kummer, so that factor is zero. Thus beta restricts to betaIntegral. Evaluate its inclusion equation on sections and apply ordinary-unit normalization and linearity to get both required torsion formulas. This proves the statement also for m=n, n=1 and zero sheaves without separate choices or division by a scalar in a module.

title: Modulus change of the derived quotient and torsion identifications
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $m,n\geq1$ with $n\mid m$, put $R_q=(\mathbf Z/q\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived scalar extension with its restriction adjunction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let
$$a_K:(K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_m)\otimes_{R_m}^{\mathbf L}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
be the canonical transitivity isomorphism of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] for the ring maps $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R_m\to R_n$. Let $F,B_0$ be abelian sheaves such that multiplication by each of $m,n$ is injective on $F$ and surjective on $B_0$. Put $H_q=\ker(q:B_0\to B_0)$ and $\bar F_q=F/qF$. Assume that $H_m$ and $\bar F_m$ are flat $R_m$-module sheaves, meaning their tensor functors on module sheaves preserve short exact sequences [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Under the quotient and normalized torsion identifications
$$F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq\bar F_q[0],\qquad B_0\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq H_q[1]$$
of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] ($q=m,n$), $a_F$ and $a_{B_0}$ induce isomorphisms
$$\bar F_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F_n,\quad \bar f\otimes\bar b\longmapsto bf\bmod nF,$$
$$H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n,\quad h\otimes\bar b\longmapsto b(m/n)h.$$
In multiplicative notation the second formula on $h\otimes1$ is $h\mapsto h^{m/n}$. The normalization is the one for which the scalar-extension unit on $B_0$ is the connecting morphism of $0\to H_q\to B_0\xrightarrow{q}B_0\to0$.
